Hello Everyone!

Hope all is well by you. I am having a bit of an issue. I am pulling data from tiingo to try and graph the last price over the course of a year. Everytime I try to graph the information I am given an error that there isn't an X value. Now, I assumed that when I see the date being pulled in it is automatically a part of the data frame.
                    UAA.Close
2019-02-27     22.52
2019-02-28     22.55
2019-03-01     22.86
2019-03-04     22.27
2019-03-05     22.31
2019-03-06     21.76

Do you know how I can somehow create these dates the value of the x axis?

Really appreciate all and any help.

All the best,

Julia

Im graphing coefficients from multiple models for 2 species of birds using small_multiple in ggplot but I'd like to have the dot and whiskers color coded based on species. Currently all dot and whiskers are the same color.

# Generate a 'small multiple' plot
library(dotwhisker)
library(broom)
library (ggplot2)
small_multiple(m123456_df_speciesfor) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
      axis.text.x=element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x=element_blank())+ylab("Coefficient estimate") +
geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = 2) +
ggtitle("Shrubland Bird") +

Bryan,

colour was hardcoded in the function to "submodel", which you weren't using.

I made a new version of the function that hard codes it to "Species". Ideally, you could submit a feature request to the dotwhisker maintainer to change this and be able to pass a colour argument through to the ggplot call.

 library(dotwhisker)
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)

m123456_df_speciesfor <- read_csv("/Users/brandonhurr/Downloads/m123456_df_speciesfora.csv") %>% select(-X1)

small_multiple_test <- function (x, dodge_size = 0.4, show_intercept = FALSE, by_2sd = TRUE,
          dot_args = list(size = 0.3), ...)
{
  df <- dotwhisker:::dw_tidy(x, by_2sd = by_2sd, ...)
  if (!show_intercept)
    df <- df %>% filter(!grepl("^\\(Intercept\\)$|^\\w+\\|\\w+$",
                               term))
  term <- estimate <- model <- submodel <- conf.high <- conf.low <- NULL
  n_vars <- length(unique(df$term))
  if (!"model" %in% names(df)) {
    if (length(df$term) == n_vars) {
      stop("'Small multiple' plots are used to compare results across many different models; please submit results from more than one model")
    }
    else {
      stop("Please add a variable named 'model' to distinguish different models")
    }
  }
  else {
    if ("submodel" %in% names(df)) {
      if (!is.factor(df$submodel)) {
        df$submodel <- factor(df$submodel, levels = unique(df$submodel))
      }
      df$mod <- df$model
      df$model <- paste0(df$model, df$submodel)
      sub_names <- unique(df$submodel)
      n_sub <- length(sub_names)
    }
    else {
      df$submodel <- 1
      n_sub <- 1
    }
  }
  mod_names <- unique(df$model)
  n_models <- length(mod_names)
  df <- dotwhisker:::add_NAs(df, n_models, mod_names)
  if (n_sub > 1) {
    df$model <- stringr::str_replace(df$model, as.character(df$submodel),
                                     "")
    mod_names <- unique(df$model)
    n_models <- length(mod_names)
  }
  if (n_sub == 1) {
    df$shift <- 0
  }
  else {
    shift <- seq(-dodge_size, dodge_size, length.out = n_sub)
    df$shift <- rep(rep(shift, each = n_vars), times = n_models)
  }
  x_ind <- rep(seq(1, n_models), each = n_vars * n_sub)
  df$x_ind <- x_ind
  if (length(x_ind) != length(mod_names)) {
    x_ind <- unique(x_ind)
  }
  point_args0 <- list(na.rm = TRUE, position = position_dodge(width = dodge_size))
  point_args <- c(point_args0, dot_args)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(y = estimate, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high,
                      x = as.factor(model), colour = Species)) + do.call(geom_pointrange,
                                                                          point_args) + ylab("") + xlab("") + facet_grid(term ~
                                                                                                                           ., scales = "free_y")
  if (n_sub == 1) {
    p <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }
  return(p)
}

I'm new to ggplot2, and i'm currently using plot_models from the package sjPlot to create a forest plot for multiple regression models.
I was following the first example here: http://www.strengejacke.de/sjPlot/reference/plot_models.html

# fit three models
fit1 <- lm(barthtot ~ c160age + c12hour + c161sex + c172code, data = efc)
fit2 <- lm(neg_c_7 ~ c160age + c12hour + c161sex + c172code, data = efc)
fit3 <- lm(tot_sc_e ~ c160age + c12hour + c161sex + c172code, data = efc)

# plot multiple models
plot_models(fit1, fit2, fit3, grid = TRUE)

Everything was fine until I noticed that the variable estimates on the y-axis were in alphabetical order. Is there a way to re-organize the estimates to the desired order for clearer presentation?

I notice that there is an argument
order.terms =
in plot_model that does this, but it does not seem to work on plot_models?

Could anyone please help? Thanks a lot in advance!

messages.body_plain:
I looked into it some.

Essentially, I think the problem comes down to the fact that the order of discrete axes need to be dictated ahead of time by the order of the factor that is fed into ggplot2. In this case, the factor is being created in the function and it is defaulting to the default, which is alphabetical. As far as I know, there is no way to change this order after the fact.

I'm happy to be wrong here, but I've not seen it.

How to get around it?
1. email the author of sjPlot and ask what the best way is.
2. hack the function plot_models() and create your own version that outputs the dataframe prior to plotting so you can make the change

Let us know how you get on.

Brandon
